louis-althusser.oneLineEn: Structuralist Marxist of ideological state apparatuses and the epistemological break.

lyotard.oneLineEn: The Postmodern Condition declared the end of metanarratives.

maurice-blanchot.oneLineEn: Explored the limits of language through literary space, the neuter, and writing of disaster.

maurice-blondel.oneLineEn: Action takes action's inner logic toward transcendence; opened modern French Catholic thought.

max-scheler.oneLineEn: Phenomenological value ethics with material value ethics and personhood against Kantian formalism.

michael-dummett.oneLineEn: Theory of meaning and anti-realism; reread Frege via assertibility conditions.

michael-oakeshott.oneLineEn: Opposed political rationalism with practical knowledge; gave British conservatism a philosophical voice.

michel-henry.oneLineEn: Phenomenology of life: life appears immediately in auto-affection.

michel-serres.oneLineEn: Joined history of science and the humanities through figures of the third and the parasite.

miguel-de-unamuno.oneLineEn: The Tragic Sense of Life wrote the irreconcilable conflict between reason and faith.

nelson-goodman.oneLineEn: Reframed induction with the grue paradox and extended symbol-system theory into aesthetics.

nicolai-hartmann.oneLineEn: New ontology mediating phenomenology and metaphysics via stratified structure of the real.

patanjali.oneLineEn: Traditional author of the Yoga Sūtras; eight-limbed yoga practice theory is systematized here.

paul-natorp.oneLineEn: Core Marburg neo-Kantian who carried epistemology into social pedagogy.

pf-strawson.oneLineEn: Individuals established descriptive metaphysics, reconnecting Kant with analytic philosophy.

poincare.oneLineEn: Conventionalism: geometric axioms are neither empirical nor a priori, but conventions.

ranciere.oneLineEn: Distribution of the sensible places politics and aesthetics in one problem-space.

raymond-aron.oneLineEn: Defended liberalism via The Opium of the Intellectuals and philosophy of history; long debate with Sartre.

rene-girard.oneLineEn: Explained violence and the sacred through mimetic desire and the scapegoat mechanism.

rg-collingwood.oneLineEn: Philosophy of history and question-and-answer logic: all history is re-enactment of thought now.

richard-swinburne.oneLineEn: Bayesian probabilistic case for theism; contemporary Anglo-American natural theology.

rm-hare.oneLineEn: Prescriptivism: moral judgments are both prescriptive and universalizable.

robert-brandom.oneLineEn: Inferentialist semantics: meaning rests on practices of giving and asking for reasons.

ruth-barcan-marcus.oneLineEn: Pioneer of quantified modal logic; the Barcan formula paved later modal semantics.

susan-stebbing.oneLineEn: Britain's first woman philosophy professor; Thinking to Some Purpose spread logical analysis for public reasoning.

th-green.oneLineEn: Source of British neo-Hegelianism and new liberalism; ethical state and positive freedom reworked liberty.

thomas-nagel.oneLineEn: Author of 'What is it like to be a bat?'; challenged reductionism from the subjective point of view.

tyler-burge.oneLineEn: Arthritis thought experiment established social externalism about mental content.

wilhelm-windelband.oneLineEn: Southwest School founder; nomothetic vs. idiographic distinction grounded cultural-science method.
